items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The names say what they do (compile_json_path_final_key, HasKeyOrArrayIndex) and there is a comment explaining why the final key is compiled differently. The formatting matches the surrounding code.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The new behaviour sits behind an overridable hook and reuses compile_json_path. Internal callers that need array indexes use a small subclass, so there is no per-backend duplication and no dead code. It matches the reference structure.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The change is small and has no error-handling paths. json.dumps quotes the key correctly. Nothing is swallowed and there are no magic constants. Hidden tests pass (F2P 2/2, P2P 78/78).

items.name: Array-index semantics kept for isnull / exact=None paths
items.name_zh: isnull / exact=None 路径保留数组下标语义
items.evidence: The shared HasKeyLookup.as_sql now always compiles the final key as an object key. KeyTransformIsNull.as_oracle/as_sqlite and KeyTransformExact.as_oracle switch to HasKeyOrArrayIndex, which keeps array-index semantics. Intermediate path segments still go through compile_json_path unchanged.
